scene.note: The chalk board becomes printed rows in straight columns, and a ticket reference is read however it was typed.

steps.note: One departure arrives: a boat's name, the hour and minute it leaves, and the seats left.
Each value goes in a column of its own width: the name on the left, the seats on the right.
Every row comes out the same length, so the columns line up down the board.
The rows are added one after another to a text that grows, each ending its line.
A line of dashes as long as the longest row goes under them.
The whole board, with its title on top, goes to the slip as one text.
A reference arrives with small letters, or with odd spaces round it from an email.
The spaces at its ends come off, and it is cut into its parts at each point.
Two references are the same whatever their capital letters, and the digits in one can be counted.
